capitals.name: Dibon (Dhiban)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Dibon, 'Mesha's hometown'. The page gives no coordinates; the dot is at the modern town of Dhiban, approximate. Mesha's 'Kir-hareseth' (Karak) is a southern town in Jeremiah's catalogue, not called a capital.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Moab (its Neo-Assyrian shape of -700 covers the whole plateau). The page gives no area; the Arnon is the biblical northern boundary, but the Mesha Stele puts Moab north of it, so the line 'was likely fluid'. Karak governorate (about 3,300 km2) is the researcher's reading for the heartland south of the Arnon. [Fixer me-04-x, 2026-10-19: the first version left Dibon (35.78 E, 31.50 N), the capital and Mesha's hometown, outside the shape for 400 years, and its -890 'loss' took Medeba from a Moab that never held it in this keyframe. Dibon is now inside (one cell, about 250 km2; the shape is about 3,540 km2). Medeba is not added to the pre-Omri shape: the Mesha Stele page 'does not say Moab held Medeba before Omri' and notes that 'in three campaign stories, no explicit reference is made to prior Moabite control', and the Moab page calls the land Mesha took 'the Israelite territory north of Wadi el-Wale with the cities of Medeba, Ataroth and Nebo'. The Omri page, by contrast, says Omri 'expanded his holdings to include northern Moab', so the pages disagree; the shape follows the stele page. The years end in -851 because the -850 keyframe starts with Mesha's conquest of Medeba.]

The Nebuchadnezzar page has 'in Zedekiah's fourth year as king of Judah (594 BC), the kings of Ammon, Edom, Moab, Sidon and Tyre met in Jerusalem' to discuss throwing off Babylonian control, and the Moab page has Moab 'later aided Nebuchadnezzar in his expedition against Jehoiakim'; neither dates the start. [Reviewer me-04-x, 2026-10-19: year moved from -609 to -605: the Nebuchadnezzar II page says the victory at Carchemish in 605 BC 'resulted in all of Syria and Israel coming under the control of the Neo-Babylonian Empire' and puts no Babylonian overlordship in the Levant before 605; 609 is the fall of Harran, not Babylon's arrival.]

ledger.note: 539 BC (bridged): Babylon falls to Cyrus. The Nebuchadnezzar II page: Nabonidus 'ruled as the last king of the Neo-Babylonian Empire from 556 to 539 BC' and the exile 'came to an end with the fall of Babylon to the Achaemenid king Cyrus the Great in 539 BC'. The 587 revolt ('In 587 BC, Ammon, Edom and Moab likewise rebelled') is on the page but its outcome is not; the Ammon page has Ammon 'a Babylonian province, shortly after being devastated by Nebuchadnezzar II in the 580s BC', so the revolt is read as crushed and Moab kept under Babylon to the empire's end. [Fixer me-04-x, 2026-10-19: replaces a vassal_end in -587 that drew Moab free for 190 years on a page that says nothing of the outcome; the Moab page has Moab 'exiled to Babylon' (Jeremiah) and no page shows Moab independent after 587.]

wars.name: Mesha's revolt against Israel

zones.text: the Israelite territory north of Wadi el-Wale with Medeba, Ataroth and Nebo: 'Omri took the land of Madeba, and occupied it in his day' and Mesha took it back; Dibon is left out because it stayed Moabite

wars.outcome: Mesha's stele claims a decisive victory and the recovery of Medeba, Nebo, Jahaz and the towns north of the Arnon; 2 Kings 3:27 says Israel's army 'withdrew from him and returned to their own land' after the siege of the Moabite capital.
wars.note: The page dates the liberation c. 850 BC; the Moab page dates the rebellion to Ahab's death 'about 853 BCE' (Thiele). The Mesha page names Jehoram but not Jehoshaphat and does not date the campaign.

wars.name: Ashdod revolt and the regional coalition against Sargon II
wars.outcome: 'In 711 BCE, Moab entered into a regional coalition with Edom and Judah in rebellion against the Assyrian King'; Moab 'avoided the direct retribution Ashdod suffered'.
wars.note: No border moved; Moab stays an Assyrian tributary in the ledger.

wars.name: Moab's rebellion against Nebuchadnezzar II
wars.outcome: 'In 587 BC, Ammon, Edom and Moab likewise rebelled'; outcome not on the page. Read as crushed (the Ammon page has Ammon a Babylonian province after the 580s); Moab stays a Babylonian vassal in the ledger until 539.
wars.note: The page also has the 594 BC meeting of the kings of Ammon, Edom, Moab, Sidon and Tyre at Jerusalem. The Moab page's 'later aided Nebuchadnezzar in his expedition against Jehoiakim' is undated. [Fixer me-04-x, 2026-10-19: the first version freed Moab in -587.]

certainty.note: The Arnon northern boundary is 'likely fluid' (Moab page); Heshbon is a border town between Moab and Ammon of ambiguous status.

notes: Cliopatria has no Moab; its Neo-Assyrian (-700), Neo-Babylonian (-600, -550) and Achaemenid (-500, -404) shapes all contain the Moab region as imperial land, so the renderer will show Moab only if this dossier's vassal and shape data are honoured over those shapes. The Moab and Mesha pages do cover David: David made the Moabites tributary (2 Samuel 8:2) and Moab was 'retained' under Solomon (d. c. 931 BC), so the kingdom-of-israel dossier's vassal_start/vassal_end moab (-1000/-930, me-04-a) is mirrored here at confidence 1 (the first version of this note said the Moab page was silent on David, which was wrong). Pre-Omri extent: the shape is Karak plus the Dibon cell; Medeba is left to Israel because the Mesha Stele page says no explicit reference is made to prior Moabite control, although the Omri page speaks of 'northern Moab'; if the renderer or a later reader prefers the Omri page, widen moab_-1250 to {region: Moab}, add back a loss of Madaba minus Dibon in -880 and give moab_-880 the Karak plus Dibon shape. Omri's conquest is placed in -880, within the reign 885-874 of the Omri page (the earlier 890 came from the stele's 'forty years' and lies before the accession). The kingdom-of-israel dossier has no Omri-era re-subjugation of Moab or gain of Medeba (matrix of the reviewer): route me-04-a. After 587 the pages give no overlord for Moab: no page opened names Moab between the 587 rebellion and c. 400 (Moab page: 'exiled to Babylon', collapse c. 400 BCE, no cause; Achaemenid Empire page: no mention of Moab or Transjordan). The fixer replaced the earlier 'free from 587' with Babylonian vassalage to 539 and Persian vassalage from 539 to c. 400, all at confidence 1, on the strength of the Ammon page (Babylonian province after the 580s, continuity into the Persian period), the Nebuchadnezzar II page (Babylon until 539) and the Achaemenid page (all the former Assyrian lands). If a page for Moab itself later shows an independent Moab in this period, restore the -587 vassal_end. The neo-babylonian-empire dossier (me-02) has no Moab event but a -609 direct gain of the Levant; Babylon reached the Levant in 605 on the Nebuchadnezzar II page: route me-02. The Assyrian end (-609) stays a bridge: the Moab page does not describe the end of Assyrian rule. Kir-hareseth, Heshbon (border with Ammon) and the Arnon line are not resolved. The page title Mesha_(king_of_Moab) did not load; 'Mesha' did. Dibon's coordinates are the modern Dhiban, approximate; the Dibon circle (10 km, one cell) is a coordinate because the place name Dibon is not in the gazetteer (listed in the report). Area: Karak about 3,290 km2, with Dibon about 3,540 km2; the Moab region about 4,050 km2; no infobox area.
